state.goal: The Can owner selected a per-tenant allowance measured in input/output tokens and immediate typed rejection of an over-budget new AI call; no waiting queue or money-based product limit. Resolve engineering details only, without changing these choices.
state.repo: No external users or compatibility obligation. Use native JavaScript/Bun with only contract adapters. This is documentation-only work. Existing native AI grammar remains. F owns outbound tenant/correlation identity; H owns AI enforcement; E owns shared runtime/transport integration. Supported SQL backends are SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL.
state.observed: Current Responses requests set max_output_tokens, but their decoder discards all usage. SystemOne requests send only model/state/questions, with no output-token cap; its decoder discards response usage and model after basic model-text validation. Native adapters have no tenant ledger, atomic reservations, input estimator or durable invocation ID. Byte limits are not verified token upper bounds.
state.provider: The current public TypeSafe API documents usage.input_tokens and usage.output_tokens in completed responses, but no request max-output-token field. Local Responses code has an output cap only. No complete-request token upper bound is currently qualified for either adapter. A technical contract can require qualification before enabling a metered profile, but cannot assert such qualification already passed.
state.failures: Fetch timeout/cancel, non-2xx, refusal, truncation, malformed response and process crash can occur after provider consumption. Non-2xx is rejected before body decoding. Missing usage cannot mean zero. Retries require separate dispatch accounting. Multiple server processes and overlapping calls share a tenant allowance; no provider I/O should hold a database transaction open.
state.criteria: Prefer auditable immediate admission, honest unknown usage, no concurrency oversubscription, durable restart behavior, explicit finite failures and bounded implementation. A hard consumption bound requires a verified bound for the entire request; estimation alone cannot prove it. Tenant/correlation identity is server-authenticated. Limit and period values can be required deployment configuration rather than arbitrary language defaults.

admission.instructions: Which admission rule best honors the selected token allowance and observed provider limitations?

criteria.qualified_bound: Atomically reserve a qualified upper bound for all request tokens before sending; refuse profiles lacking that bound, and settle to validated actual counters afterward. Strong guarantee, possibly fewer initially usable providers.
criteria.estimated_debt: Reserve estimated input plus an output allowance; charge actual totals later and block subsequent sends on any excess. Broader coverage, but explicitly a soft consumption cap that can be exceeded.
criteria.post_debit: Check current spent tokens before sending and debit only on completion without an atomic reservation. Simple, with potential concurrent overspend.

enforcement.instructions: Where should quota admission and settlement run for a tenant allowance shared by several server processes?

criteria.durable_native: At the native server provider-dispatch boundary using a configured durable ledger service and trusted tenant context; short atomic transactions bracket network I/O, with invocation IDs and idempotent settlement.
criteria.local_native: At the native dispatch boundary using each process's memory balance; simple local hooks, but restart and parallel processes do not share the same durable quota.
criteria.authored_wrapper: In ordinary Can application wrappers around otherwise unguarded native AI calls, backed by a durable ledger. The app must ensure every relevant call passes the wrapper.

window.instructions: What reset-window contract should be fixed without inventing a business-specific period?

criteria.configured_fixed: Require trusted configuration of fixed interval length and UTC anchor; assign each admitted attempt to its original half-open epoch, and settle late usage there. No allowance-wait queue.
criteria.calendar_month: Make every tenant quota reset at UTC calendar-month boundaries, with late accounting assigned to its admission month.
criteria.rolling: Maintain exact rolling-window consumption and in-flight reservations per tenant, with configurable duration and no queued admission.

unknown.instructions: After possible dispatch with no trustworthy final usage, what should happen to the admission reservation?

criteria.retain: Persist the full hold as unresolved in its original epoch; only authoritative usage or proof of no dispatch can settle/refund it, idempotently. Process exit and timeout never release it by themselves.
criteria.refund: Refund the hold on timeout, cancellation or process recovery even though provider consumption may already have happened.
criteria.charge_ceiling: Immediately finalize the entire reserved ceiling as spent on any unknown outcome, with no later usage reconciliation or refund.

counting.instructions: How should input and output usage map to the selected tenant token allowance?

criteria.sum: One unweighted pool debited by validated top-level input_tokens + output_tokens, without adding nested cached/reasoning subtotals again; provider/model identity and profile validity remain recorded.
criteria.separate: Require distinct mandatory input and output quotas, enforcing both independently with separate remaining balances.
